findings.issue: The 6max-turn-bb-raise-92o justification lists every hand ahead of the hero and leaves one out. It says 'only kings full, nines full of kings, fours full or a nine with a kicker above the four is ahead', but 9-4 (nines full of fours) also beats the hero's trip nines. This is the AC#2 spot, whose whole point was fixing a made-hand misstatement, and SPEC-08 requires the made-hand wording to be accurate.
findings.evidence: Hero 2c 9d, board 9h 4h Ks 9c. Enumerating every opponent holding with evaluate()/compareHands() against the hero's 9-9-9-K-4 gives the full houses 44, 49, 9K and KK, plus trips 9x with x in 5..A. 49 = 9-9-9-4-4 (nines full of fours) is not in the sentence: it is not 'fours full' (that is 44 = 4-4-4-9-9), and its kicker is not above the four.
findings.fix: Rewrite the closing clause so the list is complete, for example 'since only kings full, nines full, fours full or a nine with a kicker above the four is ahead'. Alternatively name 'nines full of kings or fours'. Keep 'kings full', keep the text clear of /set of kings/i, and keep it distinct for DoD#1.

findings.issue: Several rewritten no-pair justifications call the hand 'X-high' after the hero's top hole card, even though a higher board card plays. Examples: 6max-river-sb-check-qjo says 'only queen-high' on 9c Ac 6h 9d Th, where the hand plays A-Q-J with the board pair. 6max-river-utg-fold-t9s says 'only ten-high on an ace-high board'. 6max-river-utg-fold-jts says 'only jack-high' with a king on board. 6max-river-btn-fold-76s says 'only seven-high' on a Q-J board. Players understand the shorthand, but it does not say what hand the hero actually holds.
findings.evidence: The evaluator puts each one in high-card or the board's pair, with the board's ace, king or queen as the top card. For qjo the best five are 9-9-A-Q-J.
findings.fix: Say 'no pair' or 'no pair of our own' (for example 'Queen-jack has no pair of its own, only the board's nines with an ace on board'). Do not name a high card that the board outranks.

findings.issue: 6max-river-bb-check-53s ('bottom pair of fives with a three kicker') and 6max-turn-bb-check-85s ('bottom pair of eights with a five kicker') name a kicker that does not play. The best five are 5-5-K-Q-7 and 8-8-K-Q-J.
findings.evidence: Checked with handCategory(evaluate(hole + board)) and by reading the boards Qh 5c 6d 7h Ks and Kd 8h Jh Qh.
findings.fix: Drop the kicker or say it does not play (for example 'bottom pair of fives, with the board's king and queen as kickers').

findings.issue: fr-flop-bb-raise-a3o became fr-flop-bb-raise-a3s, but its justification is word-for-word the old one. changes.md says 'Every changed justification was rewritten', and §5 step 3 asks for a rewrite for the new hand. The text is still accurate for Ac 3c (trip threes, ace kicker, on 3d 3h Jh, UTG raiser), so this is a process and doc mismatch, not a factual error.
findings.evidence: A scripted comparison of old and new spots from the docs change table: this is the only one of the 72 rows whose justification is unchanged.
findings.fix: Either rewrite it for the suited hand (for example mention the club backdoor or keep it as is but drop the claim), or correct changes.md/build-log to say 71 justifications were rewritten and one was still accurate.

findings.issue: 'Adding a spot' step 2 says every hero preflop action 'must be the chart's action for that hand ... or the validator rejects the spot'. The validator, the field rule just above (A-3) and five spots in the file all allow a Minor (borderline-cell) step.
findings.evidence: golden-spots.md:85-88 says 'A Minor error (a borderline cell) is allowed'. Five of the new spots, including 6max-flop-utg-check-a9o and fr-flop-mp-check-44, rely on that.
findings.fix: Change it to 'must not be a Major error on the chart (play the chart's action; a borderline cell may go either way), or the validator rejects the spot'.

findings.issue: heroPreflopProblems runs only after buildView succeeded, so every step is known to be legal (its own docstring says so). The `if (!result.ok) break;` branch and the `as Action` cast on legalOf guard a case that cannot happen.
findings.evidence: parsePostflopSpot calls it only when view !== null, and buildView has already replayed the same steps from a deal with the same seat count.
findings.fix: Optional: keep it as a cheap guard, or assert the result instead (for example `state = (applyAction(...) as {ok: true; state: HandState}).state`). Either way is fine.

findings.issue: `expect(SPOTS).toHaveLength(RAW.spots.length)` cannot fail, because parsePostflopGoldenSpots returns every spot or throws. The SPEC-03 check is still real: the module-level parse uses real advice and throws on any problem, which fails every test in the file, and the pinned counts and checkGoldenSpot assertions are real. So this is not a blocker.
findings.evidence: parseEntries collects problems and throws if there are any, otherwise it returns all entries.
findings.fix: None required. The line could be dropped since `toHaveLength(120)` follows; the test file is locked, so leave it unless it is unlocked for another reason.

summary: The code is correct and minimal. heroPreflopProblems grades each hero preflop step with gradeDecision before advice runs (D-2) and uses the A-5 text with echo(step). The clear-cut check has its own try/catch with the A-5 message (D-3). All 288 golden tests pass and lint is clean. The tests: SPEC-02 and SPEC-05 would fail if the rule or the guard were removed. SPEC-01 rebuilds each hand independently. SPEC-03, which asserts the counts from the module-level parse instead of parsing a second time, is still a real check, because that parse uses real advice and throws on any problem. SPEC-06 covers all six bullets, and the K7o limp is confirmed Minor. Like-for-like: a script over all 72 docs-table rows found street, seats, position, board, action, multiway status and opponent stats unchanged, no unlogged changes, the order kept, and 120 spots. Fact-check: I read all 72 rewritten justifications against the evaluator category per street, the board and the replayed line with positions. That covers every line-change spot, the 10 action fixes and 92o. One MAJOR: the 92o justification's exhaustive list of hands ahead omits 9-4 (nines full of fours). The other findings are MINOR or NIT: 'X-high' named after a hole card when a higher board card plays, kickers that don't play, one justification not rewritten (a3s, still accurate), and docs step 2 overstating the rule.
